ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a rectangular frame one grid square wide. The top side has 6 small squares, and the bottom side also has 6 small squares; the left and right sides each have 3 middle side small squares, plus the four corners forming a ring of squares. The upper-left corner square has 10 written in it, the upper-right corner square has 3 written in it, and the second square from the left on the bottom side is marked x. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, the number in each square is equal to the sum of the numbers in the two adjacent squares to its left and right along this ring. Number along the square ring clockwise starting from the upper-left corner, and let the 1st number be A and the 2nd number be B, where A=10. If three consecutive numbers are a_{i-1}, a_i, a_{i+1}, then a_i=a_{i-1}+a_{i+1}, so a_{i+1}=a_i-a_{i-1}. Thus the sequence in order is A, B, B-A, -A, -B, A-B, and it cycles every 6 terms. The upper-right corner is the 6th square on the top side, so its value is A-B=3. Substituting A=10 gives 10-B=3, therefore B=7. The second square from the left on the bottom side x is congruent to the 2nd position, and also corresponds to B, so x=7.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a one-cell-wide rectangular ring: there are 6 squares along the top row, 6 along the bottom row, and 3 middle side squares on each vertical side; the top-left square contains 10, the top-right square contains 3, and x is in the second square from the left on the bottom row. Traverse the ring in order, starting at the top-left square. Let the first two values be A and B, with A = 10. Using the text rule, each square value equals the sum of its two edge-adjacent neighbors, so for consecutive ring values a_i, a_i = a_{i-1} + a_{i+1}, equivalently a_{i+1} = a_i - a_{i-1}. This gives the repeating six-term pattern A, B, B - A, -A, -B, A - B. Since the top-right square is the 6th square along the top row, its value is A - B = 3. With A = 10, solve B = 7. Then use the same six-period pattern around the ring: the square marked x is in the same residue position as the second top square, so x = B = 7.

method.method_draft: First read the image as a rectangular border of squares with an empty middle. The square marked x is on the bottom row, second from the left; immediately to its left is the bottom-left corner, and going upward along the left edge eventually reaches the top-left square labeled 10, then continuing right along the top edge reaches the top-right square labeled 3. Let the value in the x-square be x and let the bottom-left corner value be y. Propagate counterclockwise from the bottom row up the left side and across the top using the rule a_{next} = a_{current} - a_{previous}. This gives, in order, bottom-left y, then the left-side/top-left progression in terms of x and y; in particular the top-left value becomes x - y, the next top square becomes x, and the top-right value becomes -y after five more top positions. Match these to the image labels: x - y = 10 and -y = 3. Solve y = -3 and therefore x = 7.
